translation.title: A gateway, in one sentence.
translation.body:
A model gateway is a single access point to several AI models: your application calls one address with one key, and the gateway passes each request to the model you chose, then measures the consumption. The Nexora AI API follows the OpenAI API format: libraries and tools that speak that format connect to it by changing the base address and the key.

A token is the unit of text a model processes. It is what prices and consumption are measured in.

To choose between a gateway and direct access, see the guide Gateway or direct access. To call the API, see OpenAI-compatible API: change the base address. For a server of your own, see A VPS in Quebec for your AI agents.

translation.title: What the gateway does.

cards.title: A familiar format.
cards.text: Chat, embeddings (texts turned into sequences of numbers that can be compared) and a model list, with streaming, tools and response formats.

cards.title: Controlled keys.
cards.text: Each key can have a spending cap, an expiry and a rate limit. Its value is shown only once; only its fingerprint is kept.

cards.title: The location shown.
cards.text: Each model says where it is hosted, with the data policy declared by its provider.

cards.title: Billed per token.
cards.text: Prices in Canadian dollars per million tokens, input and output separate. Each request is settled at its actual cost.

cards.title: Readable errors.
cards.text: Errors follow the OpenAI format. If the model's provider is unavailable, nothing is charged.

cards.title: No content kept.
cards.text: Usage events contain only metadata: the model, the tokens, the cost and the duration.

translation.title: The location, stated plainly.
translation.body:
The hosting location shown on each model sheet comes from the published catalogue: it is information, not a guarantee of data residency. A model hosted outside Quebec processes your requests outside Quebec. Some providers announce data storage in Canada while requests are processed elsewhere: the difference between storage and processing is a question to ask. A provider subject to another country's jurisdiction can also be required to hand over data it holds, even if stored in Canada.

When data residency is a requirement, the right choice may be a system installed on your premises or hosted in Quebec: see deployment and the commitments on your data.

The guide Where your data really is explains the difference between storage, processing and jurisdiction.

Each gateway request first goes through Nexora Privacy Router, included at no extra cost.

items.title: What it does not say.
items.text: That no foreign law applies: hosting in Quebec does not, by itself, rule out the laws that apply.

items.question: What is a model gateway API?
items.answer: A single access point to several AI models. Your application calls one address with one key; the gateway passes each request to the chosen model and measures the consumption.

items.question: Is the Nexora AI API compatible with OpenAI's?
items.answer: Yes, for chat (with streaming, tools and response formats), embeddings and the model list: you only change the base address and the key. A request returns a single choice, and provider-specific parameters are ignored.

items.question: How is consumption billed?
items.answer: Per token, in Canadian dollars. Each request first reserves its maximum cost, then is settled at its actual cost from the input and output tokens; the rest is released. Without enough balance, the API answers with a payment error before any call to the model.

items.question: Where are the models hosted?
items.answer: Each catalogue sheet shows the model's hosting location (Quebec, Canada, United States, Europe or other) and the data policy declared by its provider. It is catalogue information, not a guarantee of data residency.

items.question: Does Nexora AI keep the content of my requests?
items.answer: No. The gateway's usage events contain only metadata: the model, the tokens, the cost and the duration. The model provider's data policy is shown on its sheet.

items.question: Can I buy access today?
items.answer: Not as self-service: accounts and payments only work in test mode and no real payment is accepted. For a project, write to us: we start with a diagnosis of the case.

items.question: Do I need a gateway if I use a single model?
items.answer: Not necessarily. A gateway adds an intermediary; it becomes useful when you compare or switch models, or when you want one key, one spending cap and one measure of consumption. If one provider is enough for you, direct access may be simpler.

items.question: Can I switch models without rewriting my code?
items.answer: Yes: the model is chosen by an identifier in the request. Change the identifier, keep the rest.
